description:
I’m Ahmad Ali Parr, founder and principal architect of SnapKitty Collective, an independent research and engineering initiative based in San Francisco.

My background combines managerial accounting, systems engineering, artificial intelligence, formal mathematics, computer architecture, and full-stack development. I specialize in building computational systems from first principles, connecting mathematical theory directly to working software and hardware architectures.
summary: At the lunar south pole the Sun never rises high — it circles the horizon, a few degrees up at best. This navigator compares the nine Artemis III candidate landing regions on real Sun and Earth sky geometry for a 14-day surface window (November 15–29, 2026), pulled live from the JPL Horizons system: 1,026 ephemeris rows, one Sun and one Earth table per site, every 6 hours. It scores each site on solar-power windows and direct to Earth communications windows, applies stated pass/fail guards, and recommends one site with a reason and a tradeoff per region. Mons Mouton Plateau wins: the Sun never sets across the window and Earth never drops below +11 degrees. Peak near Cabeus B loses half the window to darkness. Every number traces to a Horizons row; the terrain guard stays UNKNOWN because no local horizon profile was computed the page says so instead of pretending.
details:
We built a navigator that compares the nine Artemis III candidate landing regions on real Sun and Earth sky geometry for a 14-day surface window, November 15–29, 2026. It pulls the Sun's and Earth's apparent azimuth and elevation for each region from JPL Horizons — 1,026 ephemeris rows, every 6 hours. A C11 program reads the tables and computes, per site: hours the Sun is up, the longest continuous sunlit stretch, maximum and mean elevation, the same for Earth, then applies stated pass/fail guards and ranks the sites. It generates a page with a comparison table, one 3D sky dome per site rendered with OpenGL and GLSL, a decision ledger with a reason and tradeoff per region, and a science table of oxide abundances.

Mons Mouton Plateau is recommended: Sun up all 336 hours (max +7.30°), Earth up all 336 hours (max +11.07°). Four sites pass both guards. Peak near Cabeus B has the highest Sun max but sits in darkness half the window. Terrain is not modeled, so the terrain guard stays UNKNOWN.
projectRefs: JPL Horizons System (all Sun and Earth data)
